day-1.t: Day 1 — Know what you are adding to your site

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand what WooCommerce is and what it is not
Check your current site can carry a shop
Write down what you will not touch

b.v: About 15 minutes. Open your WordPress dashboard.

This course builds on a WordPress site you already run. You know how to publish a page and install a plugin, so we will not repeat that. Today is only about the shop layer and about not breaking what already works.
1) What WooCommerce actually is
WooCommerce is a free plugin that adds products, carts, orders and payments to WordPress. The plugin itself costs nothing, but it lives on hosting you pay for, and some add-ons are paid.

v: Free plugin, downloaded from the official plugin directory
You own the data, it sits in your own database
You are responsible for updates, backups and speed
Extra features usually come from paid extensions

b.v: 2) Check the site can carry it
A shop needs more from a server than a blog does. Look at three things before you install anything.

Check now:|Tools, then Site Health, and read the critical issues|Ask your host for the PHP version and confirm it is a current supported one|Ask how much disk space and how many database connections your plan allows|Check the site loads in under about three seconds on your phone
Do not install WooCommerce on a site that already shows Site Health errors. The shop will multiply the problem and you will not know which plugin caused what.
3) Decide what stays untouched
Write this list before you start. It stops you from redesigning the whole site at midnight when something small breaks.

v: Existing pages and their links
The theme, unless it truly cannot show a shop
Plugins you already depend on for forms or SEO
The permalink structure, changing it breaks old links

b.v: Practice
Open Site Health and take a screenshot. Write the three warnings it shows, so you can compare after the shop is installed.

day-2.t: Day 2 — Hosting, domain and the padlock

b.v: Today's goal

v: Judge whether your hosting is good enough for a shop
Make sure the padlock and https work everywhere
Set up a business email address

b.v: About 20 minutes. Have your hosting login ready.

Cheap shared hosting is fine for a small shop with a few orders a day. It becomes a problem when a sale campaign brings two hundred visitors at once and the site falls over. You do not need an expensive server, you need to know your limit.
1) What matters in hosting
Ignore the number of websites in the advert. These four things decide whether a shop runs well.

v: Server location close to your customers, or a CDN in front
Daily backups included by the host
A current PHP version, set in the hosting panel
Free SSL certificate, usually from the host

b.v: 2) Force https on the whole site
The padlock appears when the site runs on https. Browsers warn people when a checkout page is not secure, and that warning kills sales.

Do this:|In hosting, confirm SSL is active for your domain|Settings, then General, and make sure both URLs start with https|Install a free SSL plugin if the host does not redirect automatically|Open your shop page and press the padlock icon|Check there is no mixed content warning
3) Use a proper email address
Order emails sent from a free account regularly land in spam. A domain email looks professional and delivers better.

v: Create orders at yourdomain.com in the hosting panel
Set it as the shop email in WooCommerce settings
Add SPF and DKIM records if your host gives them
Test by placing an order and checking where the email lands

b.v: Do not run a shop on a free subdomain. Customers cannot see who owns it, and you cannot move it later without losing every link.
Practice
Confirm three things today: SSL is on, the site URL starts with https, and your order email arrives in the inbox and not in spam.

day-3.t: Day 3 — Install and finish the setup

b.v: Today's goal

v: Install WooCommerce the safe way
Finish the setup wizard with PKR and Pakistan
Turn off what you do not need

b.v: About 20 minutes. On the live site, but before you announce it.
Installation takes three minutes. The mistakes happen in the setup wizard, where a wrong currency or a wrong address quietly ruins every order email afterwards.
1) Install from the official directory only
Downloaded plugin files from random sites are the most common way shops get infected. The official directory is free and safe.

Install:|Plugins, then Add new|Search for WooCommerce by Automattic|Click Install, then Activate|Skip the guided tour if you prefer to set things yourself|Keep the Storefront theme option only if you need a theme
2) Answer the wizard carefully
The wizard asks where you sell and what you sell. These answers set currency, weight units and tax behaviour.

v: Country: Pakistan, currency: PKR
Weight unit: kilograms
Product type: physical, unless you sell files
Industry: choose the closest, it only changes suggestions

b.v: Do not accept the wizard's suggested paid extensions. You can add them later, and most small shops never need them.
3) Clean up the defaults
A fresh install adds sample content and marketing menus. Remove them so the dashboard is readable.

v: Delete the sample page WooCommerce creates
Turn off the inbox notifications you do not read
Remove the default dummy products
Set the shop page as the shop archive in settings

b.v: Practice
Install WooCommerce, finish the wizard with PKR and Pakistan, then open the Shop page on your phone and confirm it loads with no products yet.
Today's goal

v: Pick a theme that supports WooCommerce properly
Set the shop page layout
Keep the design boring and fast

b.v: About 20 minutes. Do this on a staging copy if you have one.
A theme is the design. It should get out of the way. Every extra slider, popup and animation adds weight and distracts from the price and the button.
1) Choose with three tests
Do not judge a theme by its demo. Judge it by these three tests on your own content.

v: Does it declare WooCommerce support
Does it load fast with your number of products
Can you remove the header video and sliders easily

b.v: 2) Set the shop pages
WooCommerce creates four special pages: Shop, Cart, Checkout and My Account. They must exist and be assigned, or checkout will fail.

Check them:|WooCommerce, then Settings, then Advanced|Confirm all four pages are assigned|Open the Shop page and set three or four products per row|Test the cart on a phone, add an item and remove it|Empty the cart and confirm the empty state looks normal
3) Keep it light
Speed is a design decision, not a plugin you install at the end.

v: One font family, two weights
Compress images before upload, not after
No full screen video in the header
Limit the homepage to three sections

b.v: Do not switch themes on a live shop without a backup and a staging test. Widgets, menus and page layouts often break and customers see the mess.
Practice
Open your shop on a phone on mobile data, not wifi. Time how long it takes to show products. Write the number down, you will compare it in Day 10.
Today's goal

v: Add a simple product correctly
Use attributes to create size and colour variations
Set stock so you never oversell

b.v: About 25 minutes. Have three product photos ready.

A simple product has one price and one stock count. A variable product has options, like size small and medium, each with its own price and stock. Getting this structure right saves you hours of editing later.
1) Add the simple product first
Start with one product and finish it completely. A finished product is a template for the rest.

Add it:|Products, then Add new|Title, then a short description and a full description|Set regular price and, only if real, a sale price|Set the SKU, your own short code for the item|Set stock quantity and enable stock management|Add the weight in kilograms|Set the product image and gallery, then publish
2) Build variations with attributes
An attribute is a property like size or colour. WooCommerce uses attributes to generate variations automatically, which is faster and less error prone than making each one by hand.

Create variations:|In Product data, choose Variable|On the Attributes tab, add Size with values S, M, L|Tick Used for variations, then Save attributes|Go to the Variations tab and choose Create variations from all attributes|Set price and stock for each variation|Publish and test each option on the front end
Do not leave a variation without its own stock count. It will show as available and you will take orders you cannot fulfil.
3) Write the description that sells
Same rule as any shop: answer the doubt, then give the details. Copying the supplier text makes every shop identical.

v: Short description: who it is for and what it fixes
Full description: what is in the box and how to use it
Sizes in centimetres, not only S M L
Delivery time written as plain text

b.v: Practice
Add one variable product with two attributes and at least four variations, each with its own stock number. Then add one of each to the cart and check the totals.

day-6.t: Day 6 — Shipping zones and delivery classes

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand zones, methods and classes
Set a flat rate for Pakistan
Charge correctly for heavy items

b.v: About 20 minutes. Keep a note of real courier rates.

A shipping zone is an area you deliver to. A method is how you charge inside that zone: flat rate, free shipping or local pickup. A class is a group of products with special shipping, like heavy items.
1) Create one zone and keep it simple
Beginners create fifteen zones and then cannot find the one charging the wrong amount. Start with one zone for the whole country.

Set it up:|WooCommerce, then Settings, then Shipping|Add a zone called Pakistan and add the country|Add a Flat rate method and type the amount|Add Free shipping and set the minimum order amount|Save and test the cart with a real address
2) Use classes for heavy items
A 200 gram scarf and a 5 kilogram machine cannot share the same delivery charge. A shipping class separates them.

v: Create a class called Heavy in Shipping settings
Assign it to the heavy products
Add a separate flat rate inside the zone for that class
Check the cart total for a mixed order

b.v: Do not offer free shipping on everything to look generous. Delivery is a real cost, and heavy orders will quietly lose money.
3) Local pickup and delivery
If you deliver by yourself in your own city, local pickup and a local flat rate are cheaper and faster than a courier.

v: Local pickup with a clear address and timing
A city flat rate for your own rider
A note that COD is available on local delivery
A cut off time, for example orders before 2 pm go today

b.v: Practice
Set one Pakistan zone with a flat rate, then add a heavy class to your heaviest product and confirm the cart charges more for it.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Cash on delivery and local wallets

b.v: Today's goal

v: Enable cash on delivery the right way
Add a wallet or bank transfer method
Understand what a card gateway needs

b.v: About 20 minutes. Test every method with a real order.
Most first orders in Pakistan arrive as cash on delivery, shortened to COD. You must switch it on yourself, because a fresh WooCommerce install only offers a few methods by default.
1) Turn on cash on delivery
COD means the courier collects cash at the door and pays you later, minus their charges. In WooCommerce you just need to enable the method and write clear instructions.

Enable it:|WooCommerce, then Settings, then Payments|Find Cash on delivery and click Manage|Enable it and rename it Cash on delivery, PKR only|Add an instruction: keep exact change ready|Save and place a test order
2) Add a wallet transfer method
WooCommerce has a direct bank transfer method. For JazzCash or Easypaisa, use it with your wallet details, or use a local plugin if one is actively maintained.

v: Rename the method to JazzCash transfer
Put the account title and number in the description
Ask the customer to send the transaction ID on WhatsApp
Mark the order on hold until you see the money

b.v: Never ask for a card number or PIN in the order notes. It is unsafe and against every payment provider's rules.
3) Card payments need a gateway

To accept cards inside checkout you need a payment gateway plugin from a provider that serves Pakistan. Each provider has its own requirements, fees and settlement time, and these change, so read the current terms before you apply.

v: Usually needs a registered business and a bank account
Charges a fee per transaction, confirm the current rate
Settlement is not instant, ask for the cycle
Keep COD running, most local buyers still expect it

b.v: Practice
Enable COD and one wallet method. Place a real test order for each, then check the order email and the order status in the dashboard.

day-8.t: Day 8 — Coupons that do not eat your profit

b.v: Today's goal

v: Create a coupon with a real limit
Know which coupon types to avoid
Calculate the discount against your margin first

b.v: About 20 minutes. Have your cost sheet from before.
A coupon is a discount with rules attached. Without rules, one person shares the code in a group of five thousand and you sell your stock at a loss in one evening.
1) Create one controlled coupon
Start with a percentage discount, a usage limit and an expiry date. Those three settings prevent most accidents.

Create it:|Marketing, then Coupons, then Add coupon|Code in capital letters, something you can say on a phone call|Discount type Percentage, amount as a number|Set expiry date and usage limit per coupon|Set minimum spend so small orders stay profitable|Publish and test it at checkout
2) Match the coupon to the goal
Different problems need different coupons. Using a discount to fix a weak product page just trains people to wait for discounts.

v: First order: small percentage, one use per customer
Clear old stock: discount on one category only
Bigger basket: fixed amount off above a spend level
Loyal buyers: a code sent on WhatsApp, never public

b.v: Do not stack a sale price with a site wide coupon without checking the final amount. That is how a Rs 1,500 product sells for less than it cost.
3) Check the maths before publishing
Write the worst case on paper: the cheapest product, the biggest allowed discount, delivery included. If that number is below your cost, change the rules.

v: Cheapest product price minus discount
Minus delivery cost you pay
Minus payment or COD charges
If the result is negative, add a minimum spend

b.v: Practice
Create one coupon with an expiry date, a usage limit and a minimum spend. Then place a test order with it and read the order total line by line.
Today's goal

v: See where people leave in the checkout
Set up a simple recovery email
Write a follow-up message that is not annoying

b.v: About 20 minutes. Check what your host allows for email.
An abandoned cart is someone who added a product and did not finish. Many of them simply got interrupted. One polite reminder brings a few back, and it costs nothing extra.
1) Find out why they left
Before you chase people, remove the reason. In Pakistan the usual reasons are delivery charges, no COD option and a checkout form that asks too much.

v: Show delivery cost before the final step
Keep the form to name, phone, city and address
Make the phone field the first one
Show the COD option clearly, with a short line of text

b.v: 2) Set up recovery
WooCommerce records abandoned carts only if a plugin does it, or through a marketing extension. Pick one that is actively maintained and read what it sends.

Set it up:|Install one cart recovery plugin from the official directory|Turn on a single email, sent after a few hours|Write a short subject line, no fake urgency|Offer help on WhatsApp rather than an instant discount|Test with your own abandoned cart
Do not email people who never entered an address. That is spam, it damages your domain reputation, and your order emails start landing in the spam folder too.
3) The WhatsApp follow-up
A message from a real person converts better than any automated email in this market. Keep it to two lines and no pressure.

v: Salam, you left the blue bedsheet in your cart
Do you want me to hold it or answer any question
One message only, no repeating
Never send before 9 am or after 9 pm

b.v: Practice
Write your follow-up WhatsApp message as a quick reply in your phone. Then abandon a test cart yourself and see whether the recovery email arrives.

day-10.t: Day 10 — Backups, updates, security and speed

b.v: Today's goal

v: Back up before every change, without exception
Update safely instead of avoiding updates
Run three free speed fixes

b.v: About 25 minutes. This is the lesson that saves your shop.

On WordPress you are the IT department. A plugin update can break checkout, and a missed update can let someone in. The habit that saves you is simple: backup first, change one thing, then check the shop.
1) The backup habit
A backup is a copy of your files and database that you can restore. Test that it restores, or it is only a hope.

Before any change:|Install one backup plugin and schedule daily database backups|Run one manual backup now and download it to your computer|Keep a copy off the server, in cloud storage|Write the date in a notebook|If anything breaks, restore first and ask questions later
2) Update without fear
Updates carry security fixes. Skipping them is riskier than updating, as long as you have a backup.

v: Update one plugin at a time, never all at once
After each update, open the shop, cart and checkout
Keep WordPress, the theme and WooCommerce on current versions
Delete plugins you do not use instead of leaving them inactive

b.v: Do not install a nulled or cracked plugin to save money. It is the most common way WooCommerce shops get malware and lose customer data.
3) Security and speed basics
Both come down to a few boring settings and one habit: keep the site small and clean.

v: Strong password plus two factor login on the admin account
Change the admin username away from admin
Limit login attempts with one security plugin
Compress images before upload, under about 150 KB each
Turn on caching from your host or one caching plugin, not three
Delete old drafts, revisions and unused themes

b.v: Practice
Take a full backup and download it. Then compress your three heaviest product images, re-upload them and time your shop page again on mobile data. Compare with Day 4.
